author: euler
content:
quirq-ai is the GitHub org behind quirq-ai/quirq, the repo I keep identical to quirq/quirq on hub.quirq.dev. My definition says you own the quirq org. Beyond that, I have no description of quirq-ai as a company or team, so I can't say more.

What's verifiable is the workspace itself: a filesystem-first content repo for quirqy, viewed with open-chat or the hub's Files tab. It has five sections (Chat, Activity, Insights, Vision, Library). Chat holds per-person tasks, each with a goal, saved chats, and a generated outcome (slides, one pager, website, or GitHub URL). Members can chat inside any conversation, and each message is committed as a .log.jsonl file.

My read, which is inference rather than anything documented: you're building a git-backed workspace where people and agents like me turn conversations and dropped files into organized tasks and finished outputs. The Vision section would be where to write it down for real.

author: euler
content:
The change is PR #11 (commit f1609f5, "Turn Chat tasks into channels"), merged into the hub's main as 8011698.

What changed: Chat is now organized into channels instead of per-person tasks. The old Chat/<username>/tasks/<task>/chats/ layout is gone. Each channel is Chat/<channel>/ with a README.md (## Input and ## Output format), chat.json plus its chat.log.jsonl, inputs/, and output/. A channel is either a workstream (hello-world, organize-quirq-repo) or a personal channel named after a GitHub login (sharmasuraj0123). Files dropped directly in Chat/ are the inbox, and I sort them into the best-fitting channel. This conversation is now in Chat/hello-world/chat.log.jsonl.

Why: the commit message and docs don't state a reason, so I can't verify one.

Correction: my earlier replies here pointed sagarrambade21 and yash-wecan to Chat/<username>/tasks/. That's outdated. Personal channels would now be Chat/sagarrambade21/ and Chat/yash-wecan/.
